newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine blue chips claw back at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine blue chips claw back at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed narrowly mixed Wednesday, with blue chips recouping midsession losses but the broad market ending a shade lower.
"Prices opened slightly higher but then eased because conditions are oversold," said Rodrigo Diz at Velox traders.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV added 0.2 percent to 790.07, while the broad market shed the same amount.

"I think these small corrections are healthy -- the market struggled to reach the psychological level of 800 yesterday and needs a breather, which shouldn't take it below 770 where there's strong technical support," Diz said.
The MerVal halted a three-day rally Tuesday with a loss of 0.4 percent and closed lower only three times in the past three-and-a-half weeks.

"We knew early on that prices would stay more or less rangebound today because volume shrank," another dealer said. "What we're seeing is a process of consolidation which may take several more days, but the medium-term outlook remains good based on rising foreign investments and strong economic indicators."
Floor volume slowed to 31.4 million pesos from an average of 40 million in the previous three sessions.
But over-the-counter deals declined only fractionally from Tuesday to 112.3 million pesos.
Winning stocks outpaced losers 30 to 25 Wednesday and 15 issues closed flat.
Top main-tier gainers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, carmaker Ciadea and petrochemical concern Indupa, up 7.1 percent, 3.5 percent and 2.0 percent, respectively.
MerVal losers were led by steelmaker Siderar, Banco Frances and cement stock Juan Minetti, which shed 4.2 percent, 2.3 percent and 1.5 percent, respectively.
